Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • The provided text corpus does not show .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, malicious setup.py logic, PEP 517 build-hook abuse, or install-time automatic execution.
  • console_scripts/CLI commands such as shux operator start, shux watch, shux daemon start, and shux install-hooks appear to require explicit user invocation and are normal CLI behavior.
  • launchd/systemd scripts are present, but README/PKG-INFO describe them as manual, explicitly confirmed setup steps. There is insufficient evidence of install-time or import-time persistence.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • **Credential theft:** scope-guard.sh references sensitive patterns such as .env, *.pem, *.key, .ssh, and .kube/config, but the code is a deny rule intended to block writes to sensitive files in a Claude Code hook. No broad discovery, harvesting, staging, or external upload evidence was identified.
  • **Network transfer/download:** README/PKG-INFO include curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celstnblacc/superharness/main/scripts/install-remote.sh | bash, but this appears to be a documented source-install path from the project repository, not evidence of C2 or secret exfiltration.
  • **Archive/staging:** shux pack export is documented as a user-triggered command to bundle .superharness/ state into a .tar.gz. It is not tied to credential collection or automatic external transmission in the provided evidence.
  • **Persistence:** macOS launchd, Linux systemd, watcher, and daemon components are present, but the provided evidence indicates documented opt-in background execution for a developer tool, not stealthy persistence registered during package installation.
  • **Lateral movement / CI-cloud abuse:** No evidence of Kubernetes abuse, CI token harvesting, cloud metadata access, Docker socket use, or GitHub Actions workflow injection was identified.
  • **Obfuscation/loaders:** Rule matches for compile, regex use, and subprocess execution were present, but the provided corpus does not show concrete base64/zlib/marshal/eval/exec-style obfuscated loaders or staged malware payloads.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The provided file list and text do not show unexplained native binaries, hidden payloads, typosquatting evidence, sudden suspicious dependency insertion, or wheel/sdist mismatch evidence.
  • README says “Current version: v1.29.0” while the package version is 1.41.0; this may indicate stale documentation, but it is not direct evidence of malicious supply-chain compromise.
